{{Top}}
{{Quote|Are we going to be using Coordinated Galactic Time here or are we going to just work with Yavin's normal day? The moon's rotation is slightly faster than that of Coruscant, so keeping on the galactic scale will put us out of sync with the planet.|[[Corran Horn/Legends|Corran Horn]]|<ref name="IJ">''[[I, Jedi]]''</ref>}}
The '''Galactic Standard Time'''<ref name="LE">''[[Lords of the Expanse]]''</ref> (abbreviated '''GST'''),<ref name="Apocalypse">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Apocalypse]]''</ref> also known as '''Coordinated Galactic Time''',<ref name="TCSWE-CGT">{{CSWECite|I|139|Coordinated Galactic Time}}</ref> '''Coruscant standard time'''<ref name="CofT">''[[Champions of the Force]]''</ref> or simply '''standard time''',<ref name="ANH">[[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|''Star Wars: A New Hope'' novelization]]</ref> was the standard measurement of [[Time/Legends|time]] in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. It was based on the [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] solar cycle.<ref name="RPG2">[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game, Second Edition|''Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game'', Second Edition]]</ref><ref name="Revised">''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded]]''</ref> The Coruscant solar cycle was 368 days long with a day consisting of 24 standard hours.<ref name="wizards">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20030403coruscant|text=Coruscant: Center of the Empire|int=Coruscant: Center of the Empire}}</ref>

Galactic Standard Time could be observed via a [[Chronometer/Legends|chronometer]]. Midday GST took place at twelve hours into a [[Standard day/Legends|standard day]], which was denoted as 12:00 GST.<ref name="Apocalypse" /> Most chronometers had a feature allowing to check local current time against Galactic Standard Time.<ref name="TCSWE-GST">{{CSWECite|I|312|Galactic Standard Time}}</ref>

==Time measurement==
{{Quote|That would be fifty-seven hours, six minutes ago, Mistress," C-3PO supplied. "Standard time, of course. If you'd prefer, I could express the duration by other time parts|[[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]]|<ref name="AoC2">''[[The New Jedi Order: Agents of Chaos II: Jedi Eclipse]]''</ref>}}
*60 [[Standard minute/Legends|standard minutes]] = 1 standard hour<ref name="RPG2" /><ref name="Revised" />
*24 [[Standard hour/Legends|standard hours]] = 1 standard day<ref name="RPG2" /><ref name="Revised" />
*5 [[Standard day/Legends|standard days]] = 1 standard week<ref name="RPG2" /><ref name="Revised" />
*7 [[Standard week/Legends|standard weeks]] = 1 standard month<ref name="RPG2" /><ref name="Revised" />
*10 [[Standard month/Legends|standard months]] + 3 festival weeks + 3 holidays = 368 standard days = 1 [[Standard year/Legends|standard year]]<ref name="RPG2" /><ref name="Revised" />

The duration of the standard month and year had been used to define the [[Galactic Standard Calendar]].<ref name="RPG2" /><ref name="Revised" /> However, [[Great ReSynchronization|calendar reforms]]<ref name="HNN 45">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|45|life/13228_2.html|RM&S; Debates Calendar Reform}}</ref> had eventually changed the Galactic Standard Calendar to a 12-month/368-day calendar.<ref name="MCBY">{{Blog|holocron|13/comments|Major Character Birth Years}}</ref><ref name="DRT">{{Blog|eeusuestornii|7|Don't Read This!!!!!!}}</ref>

Another standard time unit was the [[Standard Time Part]]. One standard day was equivalent to 1,400 standard time parts.<ref name="SoL">''[[Shield of Lies]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Although the standard year was originally defined as a 10-month year in the early [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]],<ref name="Revised" /> the keeper of the [[Holocron continuity database]] [[Leland Chee]] revealed in [[2005]] that the 10-month calendar system had been dropped for further publications and replaced by a more convenient 12-month calendar.<ref name="MCBY" /> The use of a 12-month/368-day calendar was later confirmed by [[Sue Rostoni]].<ref name="DRT" /> Thus, the reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' featured years of 12 months and months of 30 or 31 days.<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref>
